skill.name: sequenzy
skill.description: Generic guide for Sequenzy CLI and MCP operations, including auth checks, workspace management, campaign lifecycle, subscribers, sequences, webhooks, products, and operational caveats.
skill.summary: Guides agents through supported Sequenzy CLI and MCP workflows with caveats and review steps.
skill.author: Sequenzy

security_audit.summary: Static findings are largely documentation false positives: Markdown command names, example URLs, and environment variable names rather than executable code. Semantic review found real operational risk because the skill guides authenticated Sequenzy mutations, destructive confirmation bypass, and one-time secret handling.

remediation.issue: Destructive command confirmation can be bypassed in agent and CI runs.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before using --yes, deleting resources, cancelling sends, changing permissions, or mutating webhook and API key settings.

remediation.issue: API keys and webhook signing secrets can appear in agent output.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to store secrets in a secret manager, redact follow-up output, and avoid posting generated credentials in shared transcripts.

remediation.issue: The skill covers broad live workspace mutations.
remediation.suggestion: Add preflight checks for company, campaign, list, sequence, team, webhook, product, and API key operations before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Confirmation Bypass For Destructive Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to pass --yes or -y to skip prompts for destructive commands in non-TTY runs. This can delete or cancel live resources without a separate user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both locations explicitly recommend confirmation bypass for delete and similar commands. The command reference also notes that campaign cancellation has no confirmation prompt.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Secrets Can Be Exposed In Agent Output
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents API key creation and instructs agents to surface webhook signing secrets immediately. This can place credentials in chat transcripts or logs unless redacted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines cover API key creation and one-time webhook secret handling. The risk is credential exposure through agent output, not evidence of exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Authenticated Workspace Control
semantic_findings.description: The skill covers subscriber changes, campaign scheduling and cancellation, sequence enrollment, team invites, webhooks, product delivery, and API key creation. A mistaken instruction can change customer data or permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly enumerates many authenticated mutation workflows. The risk depends on user authorization, so this is a business-logic and misuse concern.

content.user_title: Manage Sequenzy Workflows With CLI Guidance
content.value_statement: Sequenzy tasks can span many CLI and MCP commands. This skill maps requests to supported workflows, caveats, and review links.
actual_capabilities: Maps broad Sequenzy requests to supported CLI and MCP workflows.
Documents auth, account, company, subscriber, list, tag, segment, template, campaign, and sequence tasks.
Explains campaign scheduling, lifecycle control, duplicate modes, and dashboard URL generation.
Covers webhook management, delivery replay, signing secret handling, and product file attachment.
Calls out unsupported immediate campaign sends and backend caveats.
limitations: It is a guide, not the Sequenzy CLI or API.
It relies on authenticated Sequenzy access outside the skill files.
Some workflows require the dashboard or direct API use.
Many examples can change live workspace data if executed.

use_cases.title: Plan a Campaign Launch
use_cases.description: Map draft creation, scheduling, test requests, labels, reply profiles, and review links before launch.

use_cases.title: Maintain Subscriber Data
use_cases.description: Choose safe commands for lists, tags, segments, imports, removals, and sequence enrollment checks.

use_cases.title: Configure Developer Integrations
use_cases.description: Manage webhooks, websites, products, delivery files, API keys, and dashboard URLs with documented caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner auth check before work starts
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this machine is authenticated with Sequenzy. If not, tell me the safest next step without exposing any secret.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a draft plan before changing live data
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Sequenzy campaign workflow for [campaign name]. Include required inputs, supported actions, review links, and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain a Subscriber List
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a subscriber or list operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me update [list name] with [subscriber source]. Validate the input, explain limits, and ask before changing live data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced mapping across CLI and MCP actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Sequenzy workflow request: [details]. Map each step to supported CLI or MCP actions, identify unsupported parts, and list approval gates.

output_examples.input: I need to schedule a launch campaign next week.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the draft campaign requirements, verifies scheduling prerequisites, asks for target confirmation, and surfaces the review link when available.

output_examples.input: Add an outbound webhook for bounce and unsubscribe events.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the endpoint, event scope, test plan, and one-time signing secret handling before any webhook mutation.

output_examples.input: Move existing VIP customers into a new onboarding sequence.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the sequence status, validates the email source, explains batching behavior, and asks before enrolling subscribers.

best_practices: Inspect existing resources before making mutations.
Ask for explicit approval before destructive or permission-changing commands.
Use dashboard URLs returned by CLI or MCP results for final review.
anti_patterns: Passing --yes to destructive commands without explicit user approval.
Assuming unsupported workflows exist because related nouns appear in docs.
Posting API keys or signing secrets into shared logs.

faq.question: Does this skill run Sequenzy commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for agents that may use the Sequenzy CLI or MCP tools.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create or schedule campaigns?
faq.answer: It documents supported campaign creation, update, scheduling, test, duplicate, cancel, pause, resume, and delete workflows.

faq.question: Can it manage subscribers and lists?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers subscribers, lists, tags, segments, imports, removals, and sequence enrollment guidance.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It references API keys and webhook signing secrets, so users should store secrets securely and avoid shared logs.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should review destructive commands, permission changes, webhook destinations, API key creation, and live campaign scheduling.
